question: Some steps happen without anyone asking: reading a conversation back, summarizing it, recording or forgetting a turn, holding an action for confirmation, opening the tool connections, and starting a sign-in. Should the product itself be named as the one doing those, or should only what a person asks for name anybody?

candidates.description: Name the product itself, and show it as the one behind every step nobody asked for.

payload.name: The Product Itself
payload.description:
The product acting on its own behalf, with nobody having asked it to. It does the housekeeping that keeps a conversation usable around whatever the person actually said: reading back what was remembered, summarizing it once it grows too long to read, recording a finished exchange or dropping one that stopped being true, holding a sensitive action until the person confirms it, opening the connections to every tool provider, and starting a sign-in the moment a service asks for one.

Not a person, and never a second user. It acts only for the person whose conversation it is, and only within what that person has already granted. Nothing it does is on its own schedule either: every step it takes sits downstream of a message somebody sent or an assistant the product added.

candidates.description: Leave them unnamed: only a step a person asks for says who asked.

context: Seven operations carry no performedBy edge: qry.loadHistory, cmd.compactHistory, cmd.commitTurnHistory, cmd.forgetConversation (agg.conversationHistory), cmd.parkApproval (agg.pendingApproval), cmd.openToolConnections (agg.toolConnection), and cmd.authorizeService (agg.serviceAuthorization). actor.chatUser is the only actor in the graph and is wired to the six user-entry operations: cmd.runTurn, cmd.runAssistant, cmd.prepareToolAccess, cmd.answerApproval, cmd.completeAuthorization, cmd.revokeAuthorization. Sibling coverage does not settle the gap. On agg.conversationHistory no sibling has an actor at all. On agg.pendingApproval, agg.toolConnection and agg.serviceAuthorization a sibling points at actor.chatUser, but the unwired operations are product-internal by their own descriptions: cmd.parkApproval is raised when the assistant hits a provider-marked destructive tool (src/conciergent/agent/runner.py:276-296), cmd.openToolConnections says "issued by the assistant run itself" (src/conciergent/agent/runner.py:196-208), and cmd.authorizeService says "issued by the connection being opened" (src/conciergent/agent/mcp/client.py:86-119). Copying the sibling actor across would assert the user triggers steps they never see. Candidate one mints actor.product and adds the seven performedBy edges; candidate two runs nothing and leaves the current split, where only user-initiated operations name an actor, as the deliberate convention.
